> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,

> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit; restated 2026-10-06 for DssHarness).** **`D-` plus TWO OR
> MORE `-`-separated segments is read as an anchor id and MUST resolve to a row here** —
> `dssharness check-anchor-citations`, the check-anchor-registry action and the door all read it so
> (✔MEASURED 2026-10-06 in a throwaway repository); `D-` plus ONE segment (`D-OPT`) is an informal
> label nothing reads, and a NEW id needs three (`anchors.minimumIdSegments`). So hyphenating a
> COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes the identifier: the always-inline row, first spelled with
> `ALWAYS-INLINE` as two segments, tripped the guard and was renamed `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE`,
> matching the `NOINLINE` segment of its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE-PER-FUNCTION-SINK`. The failure
> surfaces as “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the
> name. **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens
> for genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** (The
> full write-up was a row of the harness registry that cycle P67 retired; git holds it at `288a6be0^`.)

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. (The class row this caveat cited was a row of the harness registry that cycle P67 retired; git holds it at `288a6be0^`.)

> **THE LINE BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND HARNESS** — ⓘ HISTORY since 2026-09-16, when the harness
> registry retired and every row began filing HERE; it still explains how older rows were
> bucketed, and it still says what a production defect IS:
> **PRODUCTION** is a defect a USER OF THE COMPILER could hit -- it is in the shipped binary
> or in the config that binary reads (front end, preprocessor, semantics, HIR/MIR/LIR,
> optimiser, assembler, linker, object formats, FFI surface, diagnostics, CLI, emitted
> runtime).
> **HARNESS** is a defect only WE can hit -- tests, gates, guards, the cycle machinery,
> plans, scripts, carriages, CI, the example corpus AS a corpus.
> ⚠ `D-CONFIG-*` and `D-DIAG-*` are PRODUCTION deliberately: a `.lang/.target/.format.json`
> document IS the compiler's behaviour in this architecture, and a diagnostic is its output to a
> user. Filing either as tooling would hide real conformance defects in the harness pile, which is
> the exact thing that split exists to stop.
> ⚠ A row's bucket follows the DEFECT, never the instrument that found it: a corpus example that
> reveals a codegen bug files under codegen.
>

## Anchor Index

**Row shape: EXACTLY six cells — `Anchor`, `Priority`, `Status`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
★★★ **`Priority` IS `P0`..`P5` AND `Status` IS ONE OF `✅ CLOSED` / `🟠 OPEN` / `⏳ GATED` / `🔵 DISCLOSED` — a controlled vocabulary, added
2026-09-01 on the operator's instruction: *"add columns for priority and status ... this way
we always have clean statuses."* Before that the verdict was the FIRST GLYPH of a prose blob
that also carried the trigger, the history and the retraction, and every reader had to agree
where the verdict stopped — which is precisely the agreement that failed four times in
`check-anchor-balance`'s own comment history.
⚠ **THE STATUS CELL KEEPS ITS GLYPH, AND THE GLYPH IS THE CONTRACT.** A row is CLOSED iff its
status cell OPENS with ✅ after stripping `*_ ` — the complement defined, never the variants,
so a glyph nobody has thought of yet counts OPEN. A column holding the bare WORD `CLOSED`
would make that test false for every closed row at once.
ⓘ **The cells are what `dssharness` writes and reads:** `✅ CLOSED`, `🟠 OPEN`, `⏳ GATED`, `🔵 DISCLOSED`; a
`--status-file` holds one of them (or the bare word `closed`/`open`/`gated`/`disclosed`). The older spelling
`🔵 🟠 OPEN (DISCLOSED)` is REFUSED by the tool (✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: four rows written in it were refused
before any was applied); it survives only as history in the handoff.
★★★ **`🔵 DISCLOSED` IS OPEN WORK WHOSE DEBT PRE-DATES THIS CYCLE, AND IT EXISTS TO
REMOVE AN INCENTIVE RATHER THAN TO GRANT AN EXCUSE.** The balance gate forbids a cycle that
OPENS new debt; it does not forbid one that DISCLOSES pre-existing debt. Those are different
quantities — and while the writer could not spell the second, the cheapest way to pass the gate
was to not write the row at all: the precise dishonesty the gate exists to prevent, produced BY
the gate. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-16 at `91820d36`, which is worse than "no new row could carry it":
the six-cell migration moved every surviving disclosure claim into the `Trigger` cell while
`is_disclosed` reads `Status`, so **the exemption was reaching ZERO rows in either registry**.
A disclosed row counts in every total, files in a WORKING registry, and `--done` refuses it; it
is exempt from the net-increase FAILURE and from nothing else whatsoever.
⚠ **The claim is CHECKABLE, which is why it is a word and not a flag.** It asserts the defect
PRE-DATES this cycle, so a reviewer can look for it in the base ref. Marking a defect this cycle
introduced is a false statement about history, not a formatting choice. The word is for the reader.
⚠ **`Priority` IS A DECLARATION, NOT A SIEVE RESULT.** `burndown-queue` seeds it and then
READS it; its own docstring warns that a band is *"a sort key, not a verdict"* because a
census built from that keyword sieve reported 103 where the truth was 4. Correct the cell and
the correction survives, which re-running a sieve never does.
★ **DO NOT HAND-WRITE A ROW.** The door — `dssharness write-anchor` / `set-anchor`, and
`fold-agent` for a lane's rows; `read-anchor <ID> --json` to read a cell — takes the FIELDS and
produces the row, so a wrapped id, an unescaped pipe and a wrong cell count are all inexpressible.
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — the `check-anchor-registry` action refuses a table row whose unescaped pipes would silently drop cells.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

⚠ **APPEND AT END-OF-TABLE, NEVER AT END-OF-FILE.** This registry once carried a
second `## Anchor Index (continued)` table, which existed only because rows had been
appended past the Allowlist over many cycles; its header declared TWO columns, so every
fuller row silently lost its `Closing work` and `Cross-refs`. The 2026-08-25
production/harness split merged both tables, so each file now has exactly ONE index and
the accident cannot recur here -- but the rule that prevents it still has to be obeyed.

The correct witness is therefore NOT "tcl.h now parses": it is a strict test at the construct's own tier plus at least one header from a DIFFERENT library exercising the same construct, so the fix is proven general rather than fitted. | `D-PLAN12-TARGETSCHEMA-MULTI-SHAPE-DISCRIMINATOR-WIRING-TARGETABIMODEL-ENUM-REGISTERMACHINE` | P3 | 🟠 OPEN | **`TargetSchema` multi-shape discriminator wiring.** `TargetAbiModel` enum (`RegisterMachine` / `OperandStack` / `ResultId`) exists since ML5 cycle 2c and gates the `register-machine → stackPointer` validate() rule, but the broader discriminator role isn't documented and the per-shape mandatory-section rules aren't wired yet. Without this, the validator either rejects WASM target schemas for missing register sections (false negative) or stops enforcing register-section invariants for native (silent regression on x86_64). **Partial closure 2026-05-29 (AS1 cycle 1):** the bucket-1 reloc taxonomy half landed — `TargetRelocationInfo` + `relocations[]` + `relocationNameIndex` + `relocationKindIndex` + validate() rules for unique/non-zero `kind`, unique non-empty `name`; `formula` type-strict; `encoding.format` REQUIRED when present. | `D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL-INITIAL-EXEC` | P3 | 🟠 OPEN | 🟠 **P3 GENUINELY UNDONE — ROW WRITTEN 2026-09-16 (cycle P68, lane `cit`) FOR AN ID CITED 3 TIMES IN PRODUCTION CODE, AND NAMED IN SEVERAL SIBLING ROWS' PROSE, WITH NO ROW OF ITS OWN.** **WHAT IS MISSING:** the initial-exec TLS model — a loader-filled `tpoff` GOT slot — which is the only way to bind a TRUE LIBRARY thread-local, i.e. an `extern thread_local` whose definition no sibling CU supplies (the glibc `errno` class). **NO SHIPPED BINDING MODEL CAN CARRY ONE, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE CORRECT ANSWER RATHER THAN A GAP:** got-indirect binds ONE process-shared address per object, which is the antithesis of thread storage — every thread would alias one datum — so reaching for it would be a silent mis-bind, not a degradation. The linker therefore fail-louds with `K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport`, naming this anchor and telling the user the one thing that DOES work today: an intra-program `extern thread_local` resolves when its defining translation unit is compiled into the same program, because the definition's own `MirGlobal.isThreadLocal` drives the layout and the import is folded away like any extern data. The shipped model is local-exec only, and it covers this executable's own thread-locals. ⚠ **PREMISE CHECK:** ✔MEASURED 2026-09-16, the refusal is still live at `src/link/linker.cpp` and `src/core/types/extern_import.hpp` still documents the surviving-import case as NOT implemented; no `tpoff` GOT-slot emission exists in any walker. | **Trigger: an artifact profile that links against a shared library exporting a thread-local** — the nearer step of the dlopen/shared-library family, ahead of [[D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL-DYNAMIC-TLS]] (which needs `__tls_get_addr` / TLSDESC for a dlopen'd module's own TLS). **Closing work:** emit a GOT slot the loader fills with the symbol's `tpoff`, declare the access model in the format JSON BESIDE the existing `tlsAccess.model` local-exec verb (not INSTEAD of it — one ELF exec needs BOTH models at once: local-exec for its own thread-locals, initial-exec for imported ones, so the config shape is a second key, never a different value of `model`), and lower a thread-local extern load as `tp + [GOT]` instead of `tp + constant`. ★★ **THE WITNESS OBSTACLE THIS CELL USED TO STATE IS RETIRED — ✔MEASURED BY EXECUTION 2026-09-16 (cycle P68 round 2, lane `tls`), NOT ARGUED.** This cell used to say the row "needs a real shared library exporting a thread-local to witness it end-to-end" as though that were unobtainable. It is obtainable on this host with no new infrastructure: gcc 13.3.0 in WSL builds `libtls.so` from `__thread int lib_counter = 7;` (`.dynsym` row `TLS GLOBAL DEFAULT`, its own `PT_TLS`), a 2-pthread consumer asserting each thread sees its OWN copy RAN to exit 42 on FIVE reference builds — x86_64 PIE default-model, x86_64 PIE `-ftls-model=initial-exec`, **x86_64 non-PIE `ET_EXEC` (the shape DSS ships)**, aarch64 PIE and **aarch64 non-PIE `ET_EXEC`**, the last two under `qemu-aarch64` with `QEMU_LD_PREFIX=/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu`. **THE EXACT SHAPE TO PRODUCE, read back from those binaries:** x86_64 — ONE `R_X86_64_TPOFF64` (type 18) dynamic relocation at a GOT slot, addend 0, against the symbol, plus `DT_NEEDED`; A file no manifest LISTS — a header, typically — is checked by the editor under EVERY root manifest of its language, where the rule the build implies is "under the manifests whose listed sources include it, directly or transitively".** Left open on purpose by [[D-LSP-HEADER-CASE-RULE-NOT-WORKSPACE-AWARE]]'s closing (part 5), and reported before building rather than filled in silently. WHAT THE EDITOR DOES TODAY (`src/lsp/workspace_project.cpp` `selectDocumentConfigurations`): a LISTED document is analyzed under exactly the manifests whose expanded `sources` contain it (`core::PathIdentity` membership), under each of their pairs, with each manifest's `includes` and `defines`; an UNLISTED document gets every manifest of its language, and any diagnostic not every configuration reports is tagged `[target=<spec>, …]`. The direction is CONSERVATIVE: the includers' own configurations are always among those checked, so nothing the build would report is hidden — the cost is a tagged false alarm from a manifest that never compiles the header, and only when one workspace root holds two or more manifests of one language with DIFFERENT configurations. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-21: every one of the 9 tracked manifests is alone in its directory, and none of the repo's six multi-target workspaces holds a header at all, so no in-tree workspace reaches the over-check today. WHY IT WAS NOT BUILT, ✔MEASURED/📄 read: the editor holds include edges only for OPEN documents (their units' spliced origin buffers — and a header that contributed no rendered text is absent even there), so the exact relation needs the include closure of every listed source under each of its pairs; derived by preprocessing the project on each refresh, that costs the preprocess-splice phase part 4 measured on the 103-file sqlite speedtest1 build — 5.34 s locally and 24.14 s over UNC, for ONE pair, on every open, save or manifest change. THE DESIGN THAT FITS: an INCREMENTAL per-source include index — each listed source's include closure per configuration, RECORDED as the preprocessor opens files (not re-derived from rendered buffers, which drop a header that contributed no text), built once in the background and refreshed per CHANGED file (a changed source re-preprocesses that source alone; a changed header re-preprocesses only the sources whose recorded closure holds it; a manifest change re-plans its own sources) — never a full preprocess per refresh. An unlisted file is then checked under the configurations whose index holds it, and one no index holds (no includer at all) keeps the tagged all-manifests rule. ⚠ BOUNDARY: nested (`dependsOn`) manifests are not read by the editor at all, so a header a DEPENDENCY's sources include is checked under the root's configurations only — a separate, wider question. Trigger: the first workspace — in-tree or reported — whose root holds two manifests of one language with different configurations and a header that only some of them include. Priority: P3 (a tagged, conservative over-check; no in-tree instance). | (open) Closing work: the incremental per-source include index above, fed by the preprocessor's own file opens, refreshed per changed file; `selectDocumentConfigurations` takes an unlisted document's configurations from it. Closing test: a root with two manifests of different configurations, one source per manifest, a header included by one of them — the header is checked under the includer's configuration only, the non-includer's configuration reports nothing on it, a header no source includes still gets the tagged all-manifests rule, and editing the header re-preprocesses only its includer (counted, not timed). | Cycle P68 round 8 (lane `cr`, part 5 report-back, filed in part 6 on the coordinator's ruling); `src/lsp/workspace_project.{hpp,cpp}` (`selectDocumentConfigurations`, `resolveWorkspaceBuild`); `src/lsp/lsp_server.cpp` (`LspServer::planParse_`); `src/analysis/compilation_unit/compilation_unit.hpp` (the unit's origin buffers); with [[D-LSP-HEADER-CASE-RULE-NOT-WORKSPACE-AWARE]] (the closing that left this open) and [[D-PP-INCLUDE-RESOLVER-RELISTS-EVERY-DIRECTORY-PER-RESOLUTION]] (where the 5.34 s / 24.14 s splice figures were measured); lane `cr`'s findings, parts 5 and 6 |

No DSS ELF image defines a `__dso_handle` today (✔MEASURED: an exec that references it is refused K_SymbolUndefined; a .so leaves it UNDEFINED on x86_64 and aarch64, and glibc exports none, so such a .so would not load) — the fix needs one per image, crtbegin.o's role for gcc. | (open) BLOCKED on the ELF slice of [[D-LK-SHARED-LIBRARY-RUNS-NO-STATIC-INITIALIZERS]] — linker/image work for lane xa, not S2 of [[D-C-STDLIB-H-LACKS-THIRTY-FIVE-ISO-NAMES]] (the coordinator's routing, 2026-09-24): every DSS ELF image defines a HIDDEN per-image `__dso_handle`, and a shared object's fini array calls `__cxa_finalize(__dso_handle)` — the handle alone is not enough (✔MEASURED, glibc 2.39: registered with its own handle but never finalized, the handler still runs at exit, after the unmap, SIGSEGV 139). Then both macros pass the handle — `atexit` → `__cxa_atexit(f, 0, __dso_handle)`, `at_quick_exit` → `__cxa_at_quick_exit(f, __dso_handle)` — and so do the real ELF `atexit` / `at_quick_exit` functions for `&atexit` (C 7.1.4), which land AFTER the hook so they pass `__dso_handle` from day one (S2 does not ship them with a null handle). Pin: a DSS .so that registers a handler and is dlclose'd — the handler runs AT dlclose, not at exit — beside gcc's .so on the same host program, with a control that an exec's handler still runs at exit. | `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/stdlib.json` (the ELF `atexit` and `at_quick_exit` macros) · [[D-LK-SHARED-LIBRARY-RUNS-NO-STATIC-INITIALIZERS]] (the unload hook this row waits on; it also owns the shared-library constructor/destructor refusal, which cites the closed [[D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN]]) · [[D-C-STDLIB-H-LACKS-THIRTY-FIVE-ISO-NAMES]] (R12-F2 is its S1; its S2 ships no ELF `atexit` function before the hook) |

The mechanism (READ, not measured): `resolveMaybeAbsolute` → `rootPrefixOf` keeps the root as written (`C:/`) and `descend` rebuilds every later component with `fs::path::operator/=`, which inserts the preferred separator `\` on Windows; the resolved path is the name DSS reports. INFERRED, not measured: the same name is what `__FILE__` expands to inside the included file, which would put the mixed spelling into the compiled program's string literals — a PROGRAM-VISIBLE difference — where gcc's cpp manual documents `__FILE__` as the name by which the preprocessor opened the file (the path as written) and mingw-w64 gcc and clang are expected to print `C:/Source/…/probe1100_warning.c`; MSVC's spelling is unmeasured. | (open) MEASURE FIRST, on every Windows reference (mingw-w64 gcc, clang, MSVC) and on DSS: (1) an ABSOLUTE `#include` written with `/`, with `\` and mixed; (2) a quoted and an angled include found through a `-I`/`/I` search directory written each way; for each, the diagnostic location and `__FILE__` printed by the program (`dssharness run probe-reference-cc`, every build RUN). Where the references AGREE, that spelling is required; where they split (MSVC's backslash convention vs gcc's as-written is the expected split), it is a MEANING fork decided by the vendors' own documentation and recorded in this row. THE FIX: ONE spelling rule for a resolved include name — the resolver keeps the spelling the include and the search directory were written in for every component it does not have to correct (case-folding a matched component may still return the on-disk name), through the existing `genericSpelling` door rather than `fs::path::operator/=`, so a diagnostic, `__FILE__`, `#line` output and the depfile all carry the same name. PINS: a resolver unit test per shape above with red-on-disable, and — if `__FILE__` is program-visible — a runnable example with a `release` arm whose program checks its own `__FILE__` separator (no absolute path baked into the expected output), in both examples runners. | src/core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp (`resolveMaybeAbsolute`, `rootPrefixOf`, `descend`); src/core/substrate/path_identity.hpp (`genericSpelling`); lane `hm`'s census logs (runs 20261007-002629-68d42af6, 20261007-000625-898787ca, 20261001-155346-6b59e0da); related: [[D-PATH-MULTI-SEPARATOR-ROOT-COLLAPSED-BY-STDLIB-PATH-TRANSFORMS]]. |

(1) A DECORATION IS NOT A TYPE. gcc prints the address type of a function its header declares const or noreturn with the attribute FIRST (`__attribute__((const)) double (*)(double)`), and clang prints noreturn LAST (`void (*)(int) __attribute__((noreturn))`), a form no compiler takes as a type name, clang included. gcc and clang both compile gcc's form in a type name and ignore the attribute with a warning (gcc: "attribute does not apply to types"); DSS refuses it, which is a divergence of the C front end that the cycle's orchestrator routed to the parser's lane and is no part of this row. The census hands on the TYPE: it removes such a decoration by a CLOSED list keyed by dialect (`DECORATIONS`: for gcc `__attribute__((const))` and `__attribute__((noreturn))` leading, for clang `__attribute__((noreturn))` trailing, for cl none) -- the exact text at the end its entry names, never a pattern over attributes; any other attribute, one at the other end and one inside a type stay in the spelling and are refused by name downstream. Each entry carries what the reference itself says when that text is written there in a type name, and the self-test holds every entry to the leg's own compiler (`d-witness`) and holds that the reference's own `_Generic` takes the bare type as the type of the function it decorated itself (`d-noreturn`, `d-const`). The census line COUNTS the rows judged after a removal (`ref-decoration-dropped`) and the report names the removal per row in its last column, so such a row never reads like one judged as spelled. For every spelling the language document accepts on a later-only declaration, no reference that accepts the spelling reports the end after it (✔MEASURED, one spelling per compile: gcc 13.3.0 host run 20261008-103458-d312e33d, clang 18.1.3 20261008-101901-aa587adb, Apple clang 20261008-102007-b89d1577, cl 20261008-102043-053dbc69, mingw-w64 gcc 20261008-102051-91bcb473). THE COST: clang and Apple clang warn at four functions where DSS says nothing — a warning only; every reference that builds the program runs it to the same exit code. WHAT DSS DOES NOT CLAIM, with four of the five references: a call through a pointer object (`void (*p)(void) = first_only; p();` is reported by gcc, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc and cl; Apple clang alone sees through it), a conditional callee, a conditional with one returning arm. | `D-C-A-CALLING-CONVENTION-ATTRIBUTE-NAMING-ANOTHER-CONVENTION-IS-REFUSED-NOT-EMITTED` | P1 | 🔵 DISCLOSED | 🔵 **DISCLOSED 2026-10-08 (cycle P69 round 1, lane `cs`) — A CALLING-CONVENTION ATTRIBUTE THAT NAMES A CONVENTION OTHER THAN THE PAIR'S OWN IS REFUSED BY NAME: THE FOREIGN CONVENTION IS NOT EMITTED.** Until this round it was dropped with one warning (the unknown-attribute word), so a function declared `ms_abi` on ELF or `sysv_abi` on pe was compiled and called with the pair's own convention — a wrong call the day the other end is an object built under the named one. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-08, the language document's seven names against the four shipped pairs (`AttributeTypePositions.AConventionNameIsActiveForeignOrUnknownByThePairsOwnFacts`: 2 active, 18 foreign, 8 unknown): on x86-64 pe64 `ms_abi` is the ACTIVE convention (accepted, no effect, silent, as the references do for their own) and `sysv_abi`, `vectorcall`, `regcall`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` are FOREIGN (refused, `S_AttributeNotHonoured`); on x86-64 ELF `sysv_abi` is active and `ms_abi`, `vectorcall`, `regcall`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` are foreign; on arm64 Mach-O and on arm64 ELF `ms_abi`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` and `aarch64_vector_pcs` are foreign; a name no convention id of the pair's target document knows (`aarch64_vector_pcs` on x86-64; `sysv_abi`, `vectorcall`, `regcall` on arm64) gets the unknown-attribute warning and no effect. WHICH REFERENCES GIVE EACH NAME A MEANING (measured the same day; a name with a meaning changes the call): on x86-64 Linux `ms_abi` on gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, and `vectorcall`, `regcall`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` on clang only (gcc: an unknown attribute); on mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 `sysv_abi`; on arm64 Linux gcc `aarch64_vector_pcs` (`ms_abi` and `sysv_abi` are unknown attributes there); on Apple clang for arm64 `ms_abi`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` and `aarch64_vector_pcs` (`vectorcall` and `regcall` are reported as not supported for the target; `sysv_abi` is a silent no-op). The four x86-32 names (`cdecl`, `stdcall`, `fastcall`, `thiscall`) are ignored with a warning by gcc and clang on x86-64 Linux and are silent on mingw-w64 gcc; they are not among the seven rows. | THE CAPABILITY, NOT BUILT: compiling a function under, and calling through, a convention other than the pair's own. STAGES: (1) the convention id on the function TYPE — carried by the type lattice, with two function types that differ in it told apart by `_Generic` and by compatibility as the references tell them; (2) the callee's prologue, epilogue, argument homes and callee-saved set taken from the NAMED convention's row of the target document, not the pair's active one — the x86-64 document already holds `sysv_amd64` and `ms_x64` as rows; the ids it lists as known and unimplemented (`vectorcall`, `regcall`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all` on x86-64; `ms_arm64`, `preserve_most`, `preserve_all`, `aarch64_vector_pcs` on arm64) each need their row first; (3) every call site classifying its arguments and its clobbers by the CALLEE's convention, with each convention's own variadic rule; (4) THE CALLER-CALLEE MATRIX as tests — every convention pair in both directions, with integer, floating, aggregate and variadic arguments, through a direct call and through a function pointer; (5) the reference probe action linking a FOREIGN OBJECT, so a DSS caller meets a callee a reference compiled under the named convention, and the reverse. Until then the refusal stands, and it is loud. OPEN CELLS MET, to settle with it: `__has_attribute` answers 0 for a convention name even on the pair where it is the active convention; and no load-time check crosses the two documents to refuse a language row that names a convention id no target document knows. PINS OF THE REFUSAL: `AttributeTypePositions.AConventionNameIsActiveForeignOrUnknownByThePairsOwnFacts` and `TargetSchema.AConventionIdIsARowOrListedAsUnimplementedNeverBoth`; their mutants are among the unread ones named in [[D-C-AN-ATTRIBUTE-AFTER-A-REFERRED-TAG-NAMES-ANOTHER-TAG-AND-ONE-IN-A-TYPE-NAME-IS-REFUSED]]. (1) THE TAG FACE, SILENT: with `struct aligned { char c[64]; };` in the unit, `struct S __attribute__((aligned(16))) w;` has `sizeof w == 64` (the three references: 4); `struct T { char lead; struct S __attribute__((unused)) m; };` is 33 bytes beside a `struct unused { char c[32]; }` (references: 8); no diagnostic. With no tag of that name in scope the same reading REFUSES valid C as an incomplete type, in ten shapes (an object, a local, a parameter, a member, a union, a typedef, a pointer, a cast, a `sizeof`, and with `aligned(16)`); of the fifteen cells the references all accept with the values a plain `struct S` gives, only the enumeration one ran. (3) DROPPED WITH A WARNING: `mode(DI)` on an object or a typedef — size 4 where gcc and clang give 8; a calling-convention attribute naming another convention than the pair's own (`ms_abi` on ELF, `sysv_abi` on pe) — the convention dropped after one warning, which is a wrong call the day the two ends disagree; `vector_size` is the same class and keeps its own row [[D-C-GNU-VECTOR-SIZE-ATTRIBUTE-WARNED-AND-IGNORED]]. | FIX FOLDED with fold A1 of lane `cs` in cycle P69 round 1 (2026-10-08), in the checkpoint commit that carries that fold. (iii) WHOSE the attribute is follows gcc's documented rule — what FOLLOWS the specifier inwards decides: a pointer layer makes it the type's; the declared name, the place of a name, or a function or array declarator makes it the declared entity's; parentheses that derive nothing are looked through — and a declaration attribute written beside the name is folded per declarator as the run after the declarator is; (iv) in a TYPE position `aligned` is APPLIED (the GNU spelling in the specifier list aligns the whole named type, the C23 spelling after the base aligns the base, one in a pointer layer aligns that pointer), an unknown name is warned, `packed` is warned as ignored, and an attribute whose effect DSS cannot give is REFUSED BY NAME with the new diagnostic `S_AttributeNotHonoured`, at every position old and new — the effects table's verb `unsupported` (rows `vector_size`, `mode`, `naked`, `__declspec(allocate)`, each stating its reason) and its verb `callingConvention` (seven names, each listing convention ids; THE BOUNDARY IS EXACT: 9223372036854775808ULL is refused, 9223372036854775807ULL folds. IT FOLDS uncast; when the operand is the RESULT of an operation (`~0ULL`, `-1`, `x + 0ULL`); to `_Bool`, `double`, `float` and `__int128`; as a condition; and in `_Static_assert`, an enumerator and an array size (the CST walker). THROUGH THE SHIPPED HEADERS it refuses `(unsigned long long)(ULLONG_MAX)`, `(T)(SIZE_MAX)` and the same for UINT64_MAX, UINT_LEAST64_MAX, UINT_FAST64_MAX, UINTPTR_MAX and UINTMAX_MAX (seven constants on the pe pair). A hash seed written `(uint64_t)14695981039346656037ULL` at file scope and a mask written `~0xFFFFFFFF00000000ULL` are this shape. THE REFERENCES — cl 19.51.36260 x64 at /Od and /O2 (reference run 20261010-151340-fec14bf7), MinGW-w64 gcc 13.2.0 (20261010-151344-bb5710f2), gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64 Linux (20261010-151346-d1fa43ed), gcc 13.3.0 on arm64 Linux (20261010-151402-1be29610), AppleClang 21 on arm64 macOS (20261010-151421-4759ef0e), one program of 75 static initializers: EVERY reference folds EVERY one, and every integer target, signed or unsigned, holds the low bits of the value at its own width — `(long long)(2^64-1)` is -1, `(int)2^63` is 0, `(signed char)0x8000000000000041` is 0x41, `(int)0xFFFFFFFF80000001` is -2147483647. The seven tables differ only by their platform's own widths (`long`, the signedness of `char`, `long double`). No reference refuses anything. CAUSE (✔READ): the HIR evaluator's literal leaf holds an unsigned value above INT64_MAX in its unsigned arm, and three readers ask `asInt64`, which answers nothing for such a value — `combineCast`'s integer-to-integer arm and its arm for a wide floating target (`src/hir/const_eval.cpp`), and `combineUnary` with `applyUnaryInt` (`src/hir/const_eval_arith.hpp`). The floating arm of the same function was closed for the same hole and its comment says so. | (open) THE BASE'S DEBT. NOT BUILT IN THE FOLD THAT FOUND IT, BY THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULING OF 2026-10-10: it is the same lane's NEXT fold of the same round (cycle P69 round 1), with [[D-CE-UNSIGNED-UNARY-RESULT-NOT-REDUCED-TO-ITS-TYPE]] and before the branching filter; it closes there, before the pull request's exit. CLOSING WORK: each of the three readers takes the operand's bit pattern at its own type, behind an established domain. An unsigned target reduces modulo 2^N as it does for every other operand. A signed target cannot hold the value; where a static initializer is folded the answer is the references' — the low bits at the target's width, sign-extended. The wide floating arm takes the value as the unsigned one it is. The unary fold reads the pattern in its operand's type. A program whose optimized filter does read such a value is refused loudly, by that name; the example's shapes produce none. A function that guards NOTHING compiled, and its unwind information held NO code for the vector registers it saves (✔READ in the images of two such probes, baseline and release). A save code is not about the stack walk: it is what RESTORES THE CALLER'S register when an exception unwinds THROUGH the frame. So a handler in ANY caller — a foreign object's included — that resumed after a fault had unwound through a DSS function read a vector register holding whatever that function had left in it. "Harmless for the shipped corpus" was true of sqlite's seven functions and of nothing else. (3) THE REFERENCE'S TABLE (cl 19.51.36260 x64, /O2, reference run 20261010-124851-233ef17c, a program whose unwind codes were read from its image): prologue `40 53 48 83 ec 40 0f 29 74 24 30`, codes `@11 SAVE_XMM128 xmm6, slot 3 (rsp+48)`, `@6 ALLOC_SMALL 64`, `@2 PUSH_NONVOL rbx`; a callee that guards nothing: `@29 SAVE_XMM128 xmm6, slot 2 (rsp+32)`. The code is there in guarding and non-guarding functions alike, and the store is an aligned `movaps`. (4) THE DOCUMENTED FORMAT (Microsoft Learn, "x64 exception handling", the page dated 2019-10-14, read 2026-10-10): `UWOP_SAVE_XMM128` (8) is two nodes — the operation info is the register's number and the next slot holds the stack offset SCALED BY 16; `UWOP_SAVE_XMM128_FAR` (9) is three nodes — the UNSCALED offset in the next two slots; and for both, "the offset is always a multiple of 16", the reason given being that 128-bit XMM operations occur on 16-byte aligned memory. MASM's `.SAVEXMM128 register, offset` requires an offset "positive, and a multiple of 16" and picks the form by reach. The FAR form is therefore the far REACH, never an unaligned slot. (5) THE FRAME DID NOT GUARANTEE THAT. The saved-register area was 16-byte STRIDED and began where the outgoing-argument area ended, and that area is counted in pointer-width slots: a function whose widest call passes an ODD number of arguments on the stack saved its vector registers 8 bytes off a multiple of 16 (✔MEASURED at the base: `movups [rsp+0x28],xmm14`, baseline and release). ✔MEASURED, OUTSIDE THE DOCUMENTED FORMAT (Windows 10.0.26300, on this fold's bytes before the frame rule): a callee whose vector saves sat 8 bytes off a multiple of 16 stated each with the FAR code at its unscaled offset (`SAVE_XMM128_FAR xmm15 at rsp+104` at baseline, ten such codes in release), and the fault that unwound through it handed the caller's handler its `double` back — 42, baseline and release; with that one code renamed in the image, 1000. Today's system restores from such a slot.
